title: Union MoS Raksha Khadse reviews sports development in West Bengal; assures SAI support to strengthen grassroots sports and athlete pathways
subtitle: Inspects SAI Regional Centre Kolkata; interacts with athletes and coaches, reviews Sports Science facilities and new Khelo India hostel; discusses strengthening sports development
body_text:
Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports Smt. Raksha Khadse visited the Sports Authority of India (SAI) Regional Centre at Salt Lake, Kolkata, and reviewed the sports infrastructure, athlete development facilities and support systems available at the Centre.
During the visit, Smt. Raksha Khadse paid floral tribute at the Netaji Subhash Bust and subsequently visited the hockey field, where she interacted with trainees and coaches and took feedback on their training, facilities and competitive requirements. She also visited the indoor facilities for gymnastics and table tennis and interacted with athletes and coaches.
Smt. Khadse visited the Sports Science Department and interacted with sports science staff, reviewing the role of scientific support in athlete development, conditioning, recovery and performance enhancement. The interaction was attended by senior SAI officials, including Regional Director, SAI Kolkata, Shri Sibananda Mishra, Olympians Smt. Soma Biswas and Smt. Poulami Ghatak, Regional Director, MY Bharat, Shri Dev Kumar Chatterjee, and members of the Indian Women’s Rugby Team. She emphasised the importance of integrating sports science, nutrition, rehabilitation and performance support with quality coaching and regular competition exposure.
The Minister also inspected the new 300-bedded Khelo India hostel and reviewed the accommodation and support infrastructure being developed for athletes. She subsequently visited the archery field and athletics facilities, interacting with coaches and trainees and taking stock of their training requirements.
Following the facility inspection, Smt. Raksha Khadse chaired a review meeting with SAI officials on the functioning of the Regional Centre, including athlete development, infrastructure, coaching, sports science and support systems. She assured continued support from SAI in strengthening sporting opportunities at the grassroots and developing stronger pathways for young athletes to progress towards higher levels of competition.
Smt. Khadse emphasised that West Bengal’s rich sporting culture and talent base can be further strengthened through quality infrastructure, scientific training, quality coaching and greater competition exposure. She highlighted the importance of ensuring that young athletes have access to the facilities, training and support systems required to pursue sporting excellence.
ABOUT SAI KOLKATA
The SAI Eastern Regional Centre serves as an important regional hub for implementing and monitoring SAI schemes across West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Tripura and Andaman & Nicobar Islands. The Centre has extensive sporting infrastructure including hockey and football fields, an archery field, a 400-metre synthetic athletics track, swimming pool, basketball and volleyball courts, as well as indoor facilities for gymnastics and table tennis. It also has residential hostels and a dedicated Sports Science Centre.
